>> 00547:     async function probeRecentMaxYmd(lookbackDays = 60) {
   00548:       const base = brTodayYmd();
   00549:       const n = Math.max(3, Math.min(180, Number(lookbackDays) || 60));
   00550: 
   00551:       for (let i = 0; i <= n; i += 1) {
   00552:         const day = addDaysUTC(base, -i);
   00553:         const draws = await fetchDayDraws(day);
   00554:         if (draws && draws.length) return day;
   00555:       }
   00556:       return "";
   00557:     }
   00558: 
   00559:     const scanStartYmd = baseYmd || (await probeRecentMaxYmd(PROBE_LOOKBACK_DAYS));

   13651: /**
   13652:  * Returns the instance of the Realtime Database SDK that is associated with the provided
   13653:  * {@link @firebase/app#FirebaseApp}. Initializes a new instance with default settings if
   13654:  * no instance exists or if the existing instance uses a custom database URL.
   13655:  *
   13656:  * @param app - The {@link @firebase/app#FirebaseApp} instance that the returned Realtime
   13657:  * Database instance is associated with.
   13658:  * @param url - The URL of the Realtime Database instance to connect to. If not
   13659:  * provided, the SDK connects to the default instance of the Firebase App.
   13660:  * @returns The `Database` instance of the provided app.
   13661:  */
>> 13662: function getDatabase(app$1 = app.getApp(), url) {
   13663:     const db = app._getProvider(app$1, 'database').getImmediate({
   13664:         identifier: url
   13665:     });
   13666:     if (!db._instanceStarted) {
   13667:         const emulator = util.getDefaultEmulatorHostnameAndPort('database');
   13668:         if (emulator) {
   13669:             connectDatabaseEmulator(db, ...emulator);
   13670:         }
   13671:     }
   13672:     return db;
   13673: }
   13674: /**
   13675:  * Modify the provided instance to communicate with the Realtime Database
   13676:  * emulator.
   13677:  *
   13678:  * <p>Note: This method must be called before performing any other operation.
   13679:  *
   13680:  * @param db - The instance to modify.
   13681:  * @param host - The emulator host (ex: localhost)
   13682:  * @param port - The emulator port (ex: 8080)
   13683:  * @param options.mockUserToken - the mock auth token to use for unit testing Security Rules
   13684:  */
   13685: function connectDatabaseEmulator(db, host, port, options = {}) {
   13686:     db = util.getModularInstance(db);
   13687:     db._checkNotDeleted('useEmulator');
   13688:     const hostAndPort = `${host}:${port}`;
   13689:     const repo = db._repoInternal;
   13690:     if (db._instanceStarted) {
   13691:         // If the instance has already been started, then silenty fail if this function is called again
   13692:         // with the same parameters. If the parameters differ then assert.
   13693:         if (hostAndPort === db._repoInternal.repoInfo_.host &&
   13694:             util.deepEqual(options, repo.repoInfo_.emulatorOptions)) {
   13695:             return;
   13696:         }
   13697:         fatal('connectDatabaseEmulator() cannot initialize or alter the emulator configuration after the database instance has started.');
   13698:     }
   13699:     let tokenProvider = undefined;
   13700:     if (repo.repoInfo_.nodeAdmin) {
   13701:         if (options.mockUserToken) {
   13702:             fatal('mockUserToken is not supported by the Admin SDK. For client access with mock users, please use the "firebase" package instead of "firebase-admin".');
   13703:         }
   13704:         tokenProvider = new EmulatorTokenProvider(EmulatorTokenProvider.OWNER);
   13705:     }
   13706:     else if (options.mockUserToken) {
   13707:         const token = typeof options.mockUserToken === 'string'
   13708:             ? options.mockUserToken
   13709:             : util.createMockUserToken(options.mockUserToken, db.app.options.projectId);
   13710:         tokenProvider = new EmulatorTokenProvider(token);
   13711:     }
   13712:     // Workaround to get cookies in Firebase Studio
   13713:     if (util.isCloudWorkstation(host)) {
   13714:         void util.pingServer(host);
   13715:         util.updateEmulatorBanner('Database', true);
   13716:     }
   13717:     // Modify the repo to apply emulator settings
   13718:     repoManagerApplyEmulatorSettings(repo, hostAndPort, options, tokenProvider);
   13719: }
   13720: /**
   13721:  * Disconnects from the server (all Database operations will be completed

   00175:      *
   00176:      * @return A Promise that resolves when the current delay elapsed.
   00177:      * @private
   00178:      * @internal
   00179:      */
   00180:     backoffAndWait() {
   00181:         if (this.awaitingBackoffCompletion) {
   00182:             return Promise.reject(new Error('A backoff operation is already in progress.'));
   00183:         }
   00184:         if (this.retryCount > exports.MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS) {
   00185:             return Promise.reject(new Error('Exceeded maximum number of retries allowed.'));
   00186:         }
   00187:         // First schedule using the current base (which may be 0 and should be
   00188:         // honored as such).
   00189:         const delayWithJitterMs = this.currentBaseMs + this.jitterDelayMs();
   00190:         if (this.currentBaseMs > 0) {
   00191:             (0, logger_1.logger)('ExponentialBackoff.backoffAndWait', null, `Backing off for ${delayWithJitterMs} ms ` +
   00192:                 `(base delay: ${this.currentBaseMs} ms)`);
   00193:         }
   00194:         // Apply backoff factor to determine next delay and ensure it is within
>> 00195:         // bounds.
   00196:         this.currentBaseMs *= this.backoffFactor;
   00197:         this.currentBaseMs = Math.max(this.currentBaseMs, this.initialDelayMs);
   00198:         this.currentBaseMs = Math.min(this.currentBaseMs, this.maxDelayMs);
   00199:         this._retryCount += 1;
   00200:         return new Promise(resolve => {
   00201:             this.awaitingBackoffCompletion = true;
   00202:             (0, exports.delayExecution)(() => {
   00203:                 this.awaitingBackoffCompletion = false;
   00204:                 resolve();
   00205:             }, delayWithJitterMs);
   00206:         });
   00207:     }
   00208:     // Visible for testing.
   00209:     get retryCount() {
   00210:         return this._retryCount;
   00211:     }
   00212:     /**
   00213:      * Returns a randomized "jitter" delay based on the current base and jitter
   00214:      * factor.
   00215:      *
   00216:      * @returns {number} The jitter to apply based on the current delay.
   00217:      * @private
   00218:      * @internal
   00219:      */
   00220:     jitterDelayMs() {
   00221:         return (Math.random() - 0.5) * this.jitterFactor * this.currentBaseMs;
   00222:     }
   00223: }
   00224: exports.ExponentialBackoff = ExponentialBackoff;
   00225: //# sourceMappingURL=backoff.js.map

   00384: 
   00385: /**
   00386:  * @param P  For most requests, this should be `ParamsDictionary`, but if you're
   00387:  * using this in a route handler for a route that uses a `RegExp` or a wildcard
   00388:  * `string` path (e.g. `'/user/*'`), then `req.params` will be an array, in
   00389:  * which case you should use `ParamsArray` instead.
   00390:  *
   00391:  * @see https://expressjs.com/en/api.html#req.params
   00392:  *
   00393:  * @example
>> 00394:  *     app.get('/user/:id', (req, res) => res.send(req.params.id)); // implicitly `ParamsDictionary`
   00395:  *     app.get<ParamsArray>(/user\/(.*)/, (req, res) => res.send(req.params[0]));
   00396:  *     app.get<ParamsArray>('/user/*', (req, res) => res.send(req.params[0]));
   00397:  */
   00398: export interface Request<
   00399:     P = ParamsDictionary,
   00400:     ResBody = any,
   00401:     ReqBody = any,
   00402:     ReqQuery = ParsedQs,
   00403:     LocalsObj extends Record<string, any> = Record<string, any>,
   00404: > extends http.IncomingMessage, Express.Request {
   00405:     /**
   00406:      * Return request header.
   00407:      *
   00408:      * The `Referrer` header field is special-cased,
   00409:      * both `Referrer` and `Referer` are interchangeable.
   00410:      *
   00411:      * Examples:
   00412:      *
   00413:      *     req.get('Content-Type');
   00414:      *     // => "text/plain"
   00415:      *
   00416:      *     req.get('content-type');
   00417:      *     // => "text/plain"
   00418:      *
   00419:      *     req.get('Something');
   00420:      *     // => undefined
   00421:      *
   00422:      * Aliased as `req.header()`.
   00423:      */
   00424:     get(name: "set-cookie"): string[] | undefined;

   00088:              * ```
   00089:              *
   00090:              * The optional `byteOffset` and `length` arguments specify a memory range within
   00091:              * the `arrayBuffer` that will be shared by the `Buffer`.
   00092:              *
   00093:              * ```js
   00094:              * import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
   00095:              *
   00096:              * const ab = new ArrayBuffer(10);
   00097:              * const buf = Buffer.from(ab, 0, 2);
   00098:              *
   00099:              * console.log(buf.length);
   00100:              * // Prints: 2
   00101:              * ```
   00102:              *
   00103:              * A `TypeError` will be thrown if `arrayBuffer` is not an `ArrayBuffer` or a
   00104:              * `SharedArrayBuffer` or another type appropriate for `Buffer.from()`
   00105:              * variants.
   00106:              *
   00107:              * It is important to remember that a backing `ArrayBuffer` can cover a range
>> 00108:              * of memory that extends beyond the bounds of a `TypedArray` view. A new
   00109:              * `Buffer` created using the `buffer` property of a `TypedArray` may extend
   00110:              * beyond the range of the `TypedArray`:
   00111:              *
   00112:              * ```js
   00113:              * import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
   00114:              *
   00115:              * const arrA = Uint8Array.from([0x63, 0x64, 0x65, 0x66]); // 4 elements
   00116:              * const arrB = new Uint8Array(arrA.buffer, 1, 2); // 2 elements
   00117:              * console.log(arrA.buffer === arrB.buffer); // true
   00118:              *
   00119:              * const buf = Buffer.from(arrB.buffer);
   00120:              * console.log(buf);
   00121:              * // Prints: <Buffer 63 64 65 66>
   00122:              * ```
   00123:              * @since v5.10.0
   00124:              * @param arrayBuffer An `ArrayBuffer`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, for example the
   00125:              * `.buffer` property of a `TypedArray`.
   00126:              * @param byteOffset Index of first byte to expose. **Default:** `0`.
   00127:              * @param length Number of bytes to expose. **Default:**
   00128:              * `arrayBuffer.byteLength - byteOffset`.
   00129:              */
   00130:             from<TArrayBuffer extends WithImplicitCoercion<ArrayBufferLike>>(
   00131:                 arrayBuffer: TArrayBuffer,
   00132:                 byteOffset?: number,
   00133:                 length?: number,
   00134:             ): Buffer<ImplicitArrayBuffer<TArrayBuffer>>;
   00135:             /**
   00136:              * Creates a new `Buffer` containing `string`. The `encoding` parameter identifies
   00137:              * the character encoding to be used when converting `string` into bytes.
   00138:              *
   00139:              * ```js
   00140:              * import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
   00141:              *
   00142:              * const buf1 = Buffer.from('this is a tést');
   00143:              * const buf2 = Buffer.from('7468697320697320612074c3a97374', 'hex');
   00144:              *
   00145:              * console.log(buf1.toString());
   00146:              * // Prints: this is a tést
   00147:              * console.log(buf2.toString());
   00148:              * // Prints: this is a tést
   00149:              * console.log(buf1.toString('latin1'));
   00150:              * // Prints: this is a tÃ©st
   00151:              * ```
   00152:              *
   00153:              * A `TypeError` will be thrown if `string` is not a string or another type
   00154:              * appropriate for `Buffer.from()` variants.
   00155:              *
   00156:              * `Buffer.from(string)` may also use the internal `Buffer` pool like
   00157:              * `Buffer.allocUnsafe()` does.
   00158:              * @since v5.10.0
   00159:              * @param string A string to encode.
   00160:              * @param encoding The encoding of `string`. **Default:** `'utf8'`.
   00161:              */
   00162:             from(string: WithImplicitCoercion<string>, encoding?: BufferEncoding): Buffer<ArrayBuffer>;
   00163:             from(arrayOrString: WithImplicitCoercion<ArrayLike<number> | string>): Buffer<ArrayBuffer>;
   00164:             /**
   00165:              * Creates a new Buffer using the passed {data}
   00166:              * @param values to create a new Buffer
   00167:              */

   02008:      *
   02009:      * randomFill(buf, 5, (err, buf) => {
   02010:      *   if (err) throw err;
   02011:      *   console.log(buf.toString('hex'));
   02012:      * });
   02013:      *
   02014:      * // The above is equivalent to the following:
   02015:      * randomFill(buf, 5, 5, (err, buf) => {
   02016:      *   if (err) throw err;
   02017:      *   console.log(buf.toString('hex'));
   02018:      * });
   02019:      * ```
   02020:      *
   02021:      * Any `ArrayBuffer`, `TypedArray`, or `DataView` instance may be passed as `buffer`.
   02022:      *
   02023:      * While this includes instances of `Float32Array` and `Float64Array`, this
   02024:      * function should not be used to generate random floating-point numbers. The
   02025:      * result may contain `+Infinity`, `-Infinity`, and `NaN`, and even if the array
   02026:      * contains finite numbers only, they are not drawn from a uniform random
>> 02027:      * distribution and have no meaningful lower or upper bounds.
   02028:      *
   02029:      * ```js
   02030:      * import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
   02031:      * const { randomFill } = await import('node:crypto');
   02032:      *
   02033:      * const a = new Uint32Array(10);
   02034:      * randomFill(a, (err, buf) => {
   02035:      *   if (err) throw err;
   02036:      *   console.log(Buffer.from(buf.buffer, buf.byteOffset, buf.byteLength)
   02037:      *     .toString('hex'));
   02038:      * });
   02039:      *
   02040:      * const b = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(10));
   02041:      * randomFill(b, (err, buf) => {
   02042:      *   if (err) throw err;
   02043:      *   console.log(Buffer.from(buf.buffer, buf.byteOffset, buf.byteLength)
   02044:      *     .toString('hex'));
   02045:      * });
   02046:      *
   02047:      * const c = new ArrayBuffer(10);
   02048:      * randomFill(c, (err, buf) => {
   02049:      *   if (err) throw err;
   02050:      *   console.log(Buffer.from(buf).toString('hex'));
   02051:      * });
   02052:      * ```
   02053:      *
   02054:      * This API uses libuv's threadpool, which can have surprising and
   02055:      * negative performance implications for some applications; see the `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE` documentation for more information.
   02056:      *
   02057:      * The asynchronous version of `crypto.randomFill()` is carried out in a single
   02058:      * threadpool request. To minimize threadpool task length variation, partition
   02059:      * large `randomFill` requests when doing so as part of fulfilling a client
   02060:      * request.
   02061:      * @since v7.10.0, v6.13.0
   02062:      * @param buffer Must be supplied. The size of the provided `buffer` must not be larger than `2**31 - 1`.
   02063:      * @param [offset=0]
   02064:      * @param [size=buffer.length - offset]
   02065:      * @param callback `function(err, buf) {}`.
   02066:      */
   02067:     function randomFill<T extends NodeJS.ArrayBufferView>(
   02068:         buffer: T,
   02069:         callback: (err: Error | null, buf: T) => void,
   02070:     ): void;
   02071:     function randomFill<T extends NodeJS.ArrayBufferView>(
   02072:         buffer: T,
   02073:         offset: number,
   02074:         callback: (err: Error | null, buf: T) => void,
   02075:     ): void;
   02076:     function randomFill<T extends NodeJS.ArrayBufferView>(
   02077:         buffer: T,
   02078:         offset: number,
   02079:         size: number,
   02080:         callback: (err: Error | null, buf: T) => void,
   02081:     ): void;
   02082:     interface ScryptOptions {
   02083:         cost?: number | undefined;
   02084:         blockSize?: number | undefined;
   02085:         parallelization?: number | undefined;
   02086:         N?: number | undefined;

   00086:              * ```
   00087:              *
   00088:              * The optional `byteOffset` and `length` arguments specify a memory range within
   00089:              * the `arrayBuffer` that will be shared by the `Buffer`.
   00090:              *
   00091:              * ```js
   00092:              * import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
   00093:              *
   00094:              * const ab = new ArrayBuffer(10);
   00095:              * const buf = Buffer.from(ab, 0, 2);
   00096:              *
   00097:              * console.log(buf.length);
   00098:              * // Prints: 2
   00099:              * ```
   00100:              *
   00101:              * A `TypeError` will be thrown if `arrayBuffer` is not an `ArrayBuffer` or a
   00102:              * `SharedArrayBuffer` or another type appropriate for `Buffer.from()`
   00103:              * variants.
   00104:              *
   00105:              * It is important to remember that a backing `ArrayBuffer` can cover a range
>> 00106:              * of memory that extends beyond the bounds of a `TypedArray` view. A new
   00107:              * `Buffer` created using the `buffer` property of a `TypedArray` may extend
   00108:              * beyond the range of the `TypedArray`:
   00109:              *
   00110:              * ```js
   00111:              * import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
   00112:              *
   00113:              * const arrA = Uint8Array.from([0x63, 0x64, 0x65, 0x66]); // 4 elements
   00114:              * const arrB = new Uint8Array(arrA.buffer, 1, 2); // 2 elements
   00115:              * console.log(arrA.buffer === arrB.buffer); // true
   00116:              *
   00117:              * const buf = Buffer.from(arrB.buffer);
   00118:              * console.log(buf);
   00119:              * // Prints: <Buffer 63 64 65 66>
   00120:              * ```
   00121:              * @since v5.10.0
   00122:              * @param arrayBuffer An `ArrayBuffer`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, for example the
   00123:              * `.buffer` property of a `TypedArray`.
   00124:              * @param byteOffset Index of first byte to expose. **Default:** `0`.
   00125:              * @param length Number of bytes to expose. **Default:**
   00126:              * `arrayBuffer.byteLength - byteOffset`.
   00127:              */
   00128:             from(
   00129:                 arrayBuffer: WithImplicitCoercion<ArrayBufferLike>,
   00130:                 byteOffset?: number,
   00131:                 length?: number,
   00132:             ): Buffer;
   00133:             /**
   00134:              * Creates a new `Buffer` containing `string`. The `encoding` parameter identifies
   00135:              * the character encoding to be used when converting `string` into bytes.
   00136:              *
   00137:              * ```js
   00138:              * import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
   00139:              *
   00140:              * const buf1 = Buffer.from('this is a tést');
   00141:              * const buf2 = Buffer.from('7468697320697320612074c3a97374', 'hex');
   00142:              *
   00143:              * console.log(buf1.toString());
   00144:              * // Prints: this is a tést
   00145:              * console.log(buf2.toString());
   00146:              * // Prints: this is a tést
   00147:              * console.log(buf1.toString('latin1'));
   00148:              * // Prints: this is a tÃ©st
   00149:              * ```
   00150:              *
   00151:              * A `TypeError` will be thrown if `string` is not a string or another type
   00152:              * appropriate for `Buffer.from()` variants.
   00153:              *
   00154:              * `Buffer.from(string)` may also use the internal `Buffer` pool like
   00155:              * `Buffer.allocUnsafe()` does.
   00156:              * @since v5.10.0
   00157:              * @param string A string to encode.
   00158:              * @param encoding The encoding of `string`. **Default:** `'utf8'`.
   00159:              */
   00160:             from(string: WithImplicitCoercion<string>, encoding?: BufferEncoding): Buffer;
   00161:             from(arrayOrString: WithImplicitCoercion<ArrayLike<number> | string>): Buffer;
   00162:             /**
   00163:              * Creates a new Buffer using the passed {data}
   00164:              * @param values to create a new Buffer
   00165:              */

   00003: var toString = Object.prototype.toString

   00005: var isModern = (
   00006:   typeof Buffer !== 'undefined' &&
   00007:   typeof Buffer.alloc === 'function' &&
   00008:   typeof Buffer.allocUnsafe === 'function' &&
   00009:   typeof Buffer.from === 'function'
   00010: )
   00011: 
   00012: function isArrayBuffer (input) {
   00013:   return toString.call(input).slice(8, -1) === 'ArrayBuffer'
   00014: }
   00015: 
   00016: function fromArrayBuffer (obj, byteOffset, length) {
   00017:   byteOffset >>>= 0
   00018: 
   00019:   var maxLength = obj.byteLength - byteOffset
   00020: 
   00021:   if (maxLength < 0) {
>> 00022:     throw new RangeError("'offset' is out of bounds")
   00023:   }
   00024: 
   00025:   if (length === undefined) {
   00026:     length = maxLength
   00027:   } else {
   00028:     length >>>= 0
   00029: 
   00030:     if (length > maxLength) {
   00031:       throw new RangeError("'length' is out of bounds")
   00032:     }
   00033:   }
   00034: 
   00035:   return isModern
   00036:     ? Buffer.from(obj.slice(byteOffset, byteOffset + length))
   00037:     : new Buffer(new Uint8Array(obj.slice(byteOffset, byteOffset + length)))
   00038: }
   00039: 
   00040: function fromString (string, encoding) {
   00041:   if (typeof encoding !== 'string' || encoding === '') {
   00042:     encoding = 'utf8'
   00043:   }
   00044: 
   00045:   if (!Buffer.isEncoding(encoding)) {
   00046:     throw new TypeError('"encoding" must be a valid string encoding')
   00047:   }
   00048: 
   00049:   return isModern
   00050:     ? Buffer.from(string, encoding)
   00051:     : new Buffer(string, encoding)
   00052: }
   00053: 
   00054: function bufferFrom (value, encodingOrOffset, length) {
   00055:   if (typeof value === 'number') {
   00056:     throw new TypeError('"value" argument must not be a number')
   00057:   }
   00058: 
   00059:   if (isArrayBuffer(value)) {
   00060:     return fromArrayBuffer(value, encodingOrOffset, length)
   00061:   }
   00062: 
   00063:   if (typeof value === 'string') {
   00064:     return fromString(value, encodingOrOffset)
   00065:   }
   00066: 
   00067:   return isModern
   00068:     ? Buffer.from(value)
   00069:     : new Buffer(value)
   00070: }
   00071: 
   00072: module.exports = bufferFrom

   00344: /**
   00345:  * Assign `setting` to `val`, or return `setting`'s value.
   00346:  *
   00347:  *    app.set('foo', 'bar');
   00348:  *    app.set('foo');
   00349:  *    // => "bar"
   00350:  *
   00351:  * Mounted servers inherit their parent server's settings.
   00352:  *
   00353:  * @param {String} setting
   00354:  * @param {*} [val]
   00355:  * @return {Server} for chaining
   00356:  * @public
   00357:  */
   00358: 
   00359: app.set = function set(setting, val) {
   00360:   if (arguments.length === 1) {
>> 00361:     // app.get(setting)
   00362:     var settings = this.settings
   00363: 
   00364:     while (settings && settings !== Object.prototype) {
   00365:       if (hasOwnProperty.call(settings, setting)) {
   00366:         return settings[setting]
   00367:       }
   00368: 
   00369:       settings = Object.getPrototypeOf(settings)
   00370:     }
   00371: 
   00372:     return undefined
   00373:   }
   00374: 
   00375:   debug('set "%s" to %o', setting, val);
   00376: 
   00377:   // set value
   00378:   this.settings[setting] = val;
   00379: 
   00380:   // trigger matched settings
   00381:   switch (setting) {
   00382:     case 'etag':
   00383:       this.set('etag fn', compileETag(val));
   00384:       break;
   00385:     case 'query parser':
   00386:       this.set('query parser fn', compileQueryParser(val));
   00387:       break;
   00388:     case 'trust proxy':
   00389:       this.set('trust proxy fn', compileTrust(val));
   00390: 
   00391:       // trust proxy inherit back-compat
   00392:       Object.defineProperty(this.settings, trustProxyDefaultSymbol, {
   00393:         configurable: true,
   00394:         value: false
   00395:       });
   00396: 
   00397:       break;
   00398:   }
   00399: 
   00400:   return this;
   00401: };

   00377: /**
   00378:  * Return subdomains as an array.
   00379:  *
   00380:  * Subdomains are the dot-separated parts of the host before the main domain of
   00381:  * the app. By default, the domain of the app is assumed to be the last two
   00382:  * parts of the host. This can be changed by setting "subdomain offset".
   00383:  *
   00384:  * For example, if the domain is "tobi.ferrets.example.com":
   00385:  * If "subdomain offset" is not set, req.subdomains is `["ferrets", "tobi"]`.
   00386:  * If "subdomain offset" is 3, req.subdomains is `["tobi"]`.
   00387:  *
   00388:  * @return {Array}
   00389:  * @public
   00390:  */
   00391: 
   00392: defineGetter(req, 'subdomains', function subdomains() {
   00393:   var hostname = this.hostname;
   00394: 
   00395:   if (!hostname) return [];
   00396: 
   00397:   var offset = this.app.get('subdomain offset');
   00398:   var subdomains = !isIP(hostname)
   00399:     ? hostname.split('.').reverse()
   00400:     : [hostname];
   00401: 
   00402:   return subdomains.slice(offset);
   00403: });

   00360:  * "proxy2" were trusted.

   00377: /**
   00378:  * Return subdomains as an array.
   00379:  *
   00380:  * Subdomains are the dot-separated parts of the host before the main domain of
   00381:  * the app. By default, the domain of the app is assumed to be the last two
   00382:  * parts of the host. This can be changed by setting "subdomain offset".
   00383:  *
   00384:  * For example, if the domain is "tobi.ferrets.example.com":
   00385:  * If "subdomain offset" is not set, req.subdomains is `["ferrets", "tobi"]`.
   00386:  * If "subdomain offset" is 3, req.subdomains is `["tobi"]`.
   00387:  *
   00388:  * @return {Array}
   00389:  * @public
   00390:  */

   00392: defineGetter(req, 'subdomains', function subdomains() {
   00393:   var hostname = this.hostname;
   00394: 
   00395:   if (!hostname) return [];
   00396: 
   00397:   var offset = this.app.get('subdomain offset');
   00398:   var subdomains = !isIP(hostname)
   00399:     ? hostname.split('.').reverse()
   00400:     : [hostname];
   00401: 
   00402:   return subdomains.slice(offset);
   00403: });

   00416: /**
   00417:  * Parse the "Host" header field to a hostname.
   00418:  *
   00419:  * When the "trust proxy" setting trusts the socket
   00420:  * address, the "X-Forwarded-Host" header field will
   00421:  * be trusted.

   00423:  * @return {String}
   00424:  * @public
   00425:  */
   00426: 
   00427: defineGetter(req, 'hostname', function hostname(){
   00428:   var trust = this.app.get('trust proxy fn');
   00429:   var host = this.get('X-Forwarded-Host');
   00430: 
   00431:   if (!host || !trust(this.connection.remoteAddress, 0)) {
   00432:     host = this.get('Host');
   00433:   } else if (host.indexOf(',') !== -1) {
   00434:     // Note: X-Forwarded-Host is normally only ever a
   00435:     //       single value, but this is to be safe.
   00436:     host = host.substring(0, host.indexOf(',')).trimRight()
   00437:   }
   00438: 
   00439:   if (!host) return;
   00440: 
   00441:   // IPv6 literal support
   00442:   var offset = host[0] === '['
   00443:     ? host.indexOf(']') + 1
   00444:     : 0;
   00445:   var index = host.indexOf(':', offset);
   00446: 
   00447:   return index !== -1
   00448:     ? host.substring(0, index)
   00449:     : host;
   00450: });
   00451:

   00458: /**
   00459:  * Check if the request is fresh, aka
   00460:  * Last-Modified and/or the ETag
   00461:  * still match.
   00462:  *
   00463:  * @return {Boolean}
   00464:  * @public

   00467: defineGetter(req, 'fresh', function(){
   00468:   var method = this.method;
   00469:   var res = this.res
   00470:   var status = res.statusCode
   00471: 
   00472:   // GET or HEAD for weak freshness validation only
   00473:   if ('GET' !== method && 'HEAD' !== method) return false;
   00474: 
   00475:   // 2xx or 304 as per rfc2616 14.26
   00476:   if ((status >= 200 && status < 300) || 304 === status) {
   00477:     return fresh(this.headers, {
   00478:       'etag': res.get('ETag'),
   00479:       'last-modified': res.get('Last-Modified')
   00480:     })
   00481:   }
   00482: 
   00483:   return false;

   00383:  * or when an error occurs. Be sure to check `res.headersSent`
   00384:  * if you wish to attempt responding, as the header and some data
   00385:  * may have already been transferred.
   00386:  *
   00387:  * Options:
   00388:  *
   00389:  *   - `maxAge`   defaulting to 0 (can be string converted by `ms`)
   00390:  *   - `root`     root directory for relative filenames
   00391:  *   - `headers`  object of headers to serve with file
   00392:  *   - `dotfiles` serve dotfiles, defaulting to false; can be `"allow"` to send them
   00393:  *
   00394:  * Other options are passed along to `send`.
   00395:  *
   00396:  * Examples:
   00397:  *
   00398:  *  The following example illustrates how `res.sendFile()` may
   00399:  *  be used as an alternative for the `static()` middleware for
   00400:  *  dynamic situations. The code backing `res.sendFile()` is actually
   00401:  *  the same code, so HTTP cache support etc is identical.
   00402:  *
>> 00403:  *     app.get('/user/:uid/photos/:file', function(req, res){
   00404:  *       var uid = req.params.uid
   00405:  *         , file = req.params.file;
   00406:  *

   00408:  *         if (yes) {
   00409:  *           res.sendFile('/uploads/' + uid + '/' + file);
   00410:  *         } else {

   00418: 
   00419: res.sendFile = function sendFile(path, options, callback) {
   00420:   var done = callback;
   00421:   var req = this.req;
   00422:   var res = this;
   00423:   var next = req.next;
   00424:   var opts = options || {};
   00425: 
   00426:   if (!path) {
   00427:     throw new TypeError('path argument is required to res.sendFile');
   00428:   }
   00429: 
   00430:   if (typeof path !== 'string') {
   00431:     throw new TypeError('path must be a string to res.sendFile')
   00432:   }
   00433: 
   00434:   // support function as second arg
   00435:   if (typeof options === 'function') {
   00436:     done = options;
   00437:     opts = {};
   00438:   }
   00439: 
   00440:   if (!opts.root && !isAbsolute(path)) {
   00441:     throw new TypeError('path must be absolute or specify root to res.sendFile');
   00442:   }
   00443: 
   00444:   // create file stream
   00445:   var pathname = encodeURI(path);
   00446:   var file = send(req, pathname, opts);
   00447: 
   00448:   // transfer
   00449:   sendfile(res, file, opts, function (err) {
   00450:     if (done) return done(err);
   00451:     if (err && err.code === 'EISDIR') return next();
   00452: 
   00453:     // next() all but write errors
   00454:     if (err && err.code !== 'ECONNABORTED' && err.syscall !== 'write') {
   00455:       next(err);
   00456:     }
   00457:   });
   00458: };

   00174:         }

   00176:             this.certType = 'sha256';

   00054: /**
   00055:  * Gets the download URL for the given {@link https://cloud.google.com/nodejs/docs/reference/storage/latest/storage/file | File}.
   00056:  *
   00057:  * @example
   00058:  * ```javascript
   00059:  * // Get the downloadUrl for a given file ref
   00060:  * const storage = getStorage();
   00061:  * const myRef = ref(storage, 'images/mountains.jpg');
   00062:  * const downloadUrl = await getDownloadURL(myRef);
   00063:  * ```
   00064:  */
   00065: async function getDownloadURL(file) {
   00066:     const endpoint = (process.env.STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST ||
   00067:         'https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com') + '/v0';
   00068:     const { downloadTokens } = await (0, utils_1.getFirebaseMetadata)(endpoint, file);
   00069:     if (!downloadTokens) {
   00070:         throw new error_1.FirebaseError({
   00071:             code: 'storage/no-download-token',
   00072:             message: 'No download token available. Please create one in the Firebase Console.',
   00073:         });
   00074:     }
   00075:     const [token] = downloadTokens.split(',');
   00076:     return `${endpoint}/b/${file.bucket.name}/o/${encodeURIComponent(file.name)}?alt=media&token=${token}`;
   00077: }

   00065:  * @private
   00066:  * @param {Array} array The array to inspect.
   00067:  * @param {Function} predicate The function invoked per iteration.
   00068:  * @param {number} fromIndex The index to search from.
   00069:  * @param {boolean} [fromRight] Specify iterating from right to left.
   00070:  * @returns {number} Returns the index of the matched value, else `-1`.
   00071:  */
   00072: function baseFindIndex(array, predicate, fromIndex, fromRight) {
   00073:   var length = array.length,
   00074:       index = fromIndex + (fromRight ? 1 : -1);
   00075: 
   00076:   while ((fromRight ? index-- : ++index < length)) {
   00077:     if (predicate(array[index], index, array)) {
   00078:       return index;
   00079:     }
   00080:   }
   00081:   return -1;
   00082: }
   00083: 
   00084: /**
>> 00085:  * The base implementation of `_.indexOf` without `fromIndex` bounds checks.
   00086:  *
   00087:  * @private
   00088:  * @param {Array} array The array to inspect.
   00089:  * @param {*} value The value to search for.
   00090:  * @param {number} fromIndex The index to search from.
   00091:  * @returns {number} Returns the index of the matched value, else `-1`.
   00092:  */
   00093: function baseIndexOf(array, value, fromIndex) {
   00094:   if (value !== value) {
   00095:     return baseFindIndex(array, baseIsNaN, fromIndex);
   00096:   }
   00097:   var index = fromIndex - 1,
   00098:       length = array.length;
   00099: 
   00100:   while (++index < length) {
   00101:     if (array[index] === value) {
   00102:       return index;
   00103:     }
   00104:   }
   00105:   return -1;
   00106: }
   00107: 
   00108: /**
   00109:  * The base implementation of `_.isNaN` without support for number objects.
   00110:  *
   00111:  * @private
   00112:  * @param {*} value The value to check.
   00113:  * @returns {boolean} Returns `true` if `value` is `NaN`, else `false`.
   00114:  */
   00115: function baseIsNaN(value) {
   00116:   return value !== value;
   00117: }
   00118: 
   00119: /**
   00120:  * The base implementation of `_.times` without support for iteratee shorthands
   00121:  * or max array length checks.
   00122:  *
   00123:  * @private
   00124:  * @param {number} n The number of times to invoke `iteratee`.
   00125:  * @param {Function} iteratee The function invoked per iteration.
   00126:  * @returns {Array} Returns the array of results.
   00127:  */
   00128: function baseTimes(n, iteratee) {
   00129:   var index = -1,
   00130:       result = Array(n);
   00131: 
   00132:   while (++index < n) {
   00133:     result[index] = iteratee(index);
   00134:   }

   00264: /**
